papers_read.title_as_printed: Attention-Guided Autoencoder for Automated Progression Prediction of Subjective Cognitive Decline with Structural MRI (Guan, Yue, Yap, Xiao, Bozoki, Liu; IEEE J Biomed Health Inform 2023, 27(6):2980-2989; author manuscript)
Random forest model for feature-based Alzheimer's disease conversion prediction from early mild cognitive impairment subjects (Velazquez, Lee; PLoS ONE 16(4): e0244773, 2021)

what_each_reports.P-229: Primary task: progressive vs stable subjective cognitive decline (SCD converting to MCI within 84 months) in the private CLAS cohort (24 pSCD / 52 sSCD), 90 AAL grey-matter ROI volumes from T1 MRI, domain-transfer autoencoder trained on ADNI AD (159) / NC (201) with unlabelled CLAS SCD. IADT: accuracy 71.05%, balanced accuracy 69.87%, specificity 73.08%. A secondary MCI-conversion experiment (393 ADNI MCI, 167 pMCI / 226 sMCI, 36 months) is reported in Table IV, whose numbers do not survive in the text extract.
what_each_reports.P-178: Early MCI (EMCI) only, ADNI-1/2/GO: 49 eventual converters (mean time to AD 5.02 years, up to 12 years in study) vs 334 non-converters; nine features (age, race, APOE4, hippocampal and ventricular volume, ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE); visit-level records (1806 visits) randomly oversampled to 1608 per class and split 1206/402 per class; 1000-tree random forest. Accuracy 93.6%, AUC 0.96 (9 features). SVC on the same data reaches 90.0% accuracy with AUC 0.54, i.e. majority-class performance.

quantity_a: Accuracy of classifying progressive vs stable SCD (conversion to MCI within 7 years) in a 76-person Chinese community cohort, from MRI grey-matter ROI volumes, with the classifier trained on ADNI AD vs NC (cross-domain transfer, CLAS labels unseen in training).
quantity_b: Accuracy of classifying ADNI early-MCI visits as eventual AD converters vs non-converters (no fixed horizon; mean 5 years), from demographics, APOE4, cognitive scores and two MRI volumes, random split of oversampled visit records.
incompatible_if_same: Not assessable as the same quantity. Even on a shared task, a 71% and a 94% accuracy from different methods, with neither study testing the other's method or claiming an ordering the other refutes, would not be incompatible.

gates.task: mismatch: P-229's 71.05% is SCD-to-MCI progression (a preclinical transition), not MCI-to-AD conversion; P-178 is EMCI-to-AD conversion. The record's T2 for P-229 is wrong for the figure it quotes
gates.dataset_family: mismatch for the quoted figures: P-229's 71.05% is tested on CLAS (a private Shanghai cohort; ADNI only supplies the AD/NC training data), P-178 is ADNI
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-229 is a cross-cohort transfer test (trained on ADNI, tested on CLAS); P-178 is a random split within ADNI visit records
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-229 uses MRI ROI volumes only; P-178 uses mainly clinical/cognitive features plus two MRI volumes; the record sets modality_family_equal 'No'

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both report accuracy, but on different transitions (SCD to MCI within 84 months vs EMCI to AD at any time), different populations and different units of analysis (P-178 splits oversampled visit records, not subjects, so the same person's visits and their duplicates can appear in training and test sets).
performance_validity: The automatic flag is not tripped (93.6% accuracy, AUC 0.96, both below 0.97; pack: performance_suspect false). But P-178's accuracy sits against an 87% majority-class baseline (its SVC reaches 90.0% with AUC 0.54), and it has no external cohort. Not decisive here because the quantities differ.
independence: Distinct author groups (UNC/Shanghai Mental Health Center vs University of Missouri-Kansas City); P-229's training data and P-178 both come from ADNI.
grounds: P-229's 71.05% is the accuracy for predicting which people with subjective cognitive decline progress to MCI within 84 months in the CLAS cohort, whereas P-178's 93.6% is for predicting which ADNI early-MCI patients eventually convert to AD, so the transitions, populations and horizons differ.

The predictor sets differ (MRI grey-matter ROI volumes only vs a clinical/cognitive feature set with two MRI volumes), and so does the evaluation (a cross-cohort transfer test vs a random split of oversampled visit records).
The dataset-family, task and modality gates all fail for the figures quoted, and no waiver is on record.
P-229's own MCI-conversion result (Table IV) cannot be read from the extract, so no like-for-like MCI-to-AD comparison is available from P-229.

evidence_quotes.quote: This dataset includes 76 SCD subjects with 3T T1-weighted structural MRIs. There are 24 progressive SCD (pSCD) and 52 stable SCD (sSCD) subjects. These pSCD subjects have evolved to MCI within the next 84 months
our model achieves higher accuracy, balanced accuracy (i.e., 71.05%, 69.87%) and specificity (i.e., 73.08%) which are much better than the other three state-of-the-art methods
In our experiment, we use the ADNI dataset as the source domain, while the CLAS dataset is used as the target domain.

383 Early Mild Cognitive Impairment (EMCI) patients were gathered from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Of these patients, 49 would eventually convert to AD (EMCI_C), whereas the remaining 334 did not convert (EMCI_NC).
our 9-feature random forest implementation with an accuracy of 93.6% and an AUC of 96% against a 383-patient data set represents our best model.
Record# after Oversampling 1608 1608 Training Data 1206 1206 Testing Data 402 402 (Table 1)

record_defects: claim_a 'P-229: Acc 71.05 on T2' mislabels the task: 71.05% is the pSCD vs sSCD (SCD-to-MCI, CLAS) accuracy, not an MCI-to-AD conversion result.
dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong for the quoted figures: P-229's 71.05% is measured on CLAS, not ADNI.
claim_b 'Acc 93.6 on T2' omits that it is an EMCI-only cohort with no fixed horizon (mean 5.02 years to conversion), evaluated on oversampled visit records, not subjects.
Registry Sample_N_Approx '393' for P-229 corresponds to its secondary MCI experiment; the quoted accuracy comes from the 76-subject CLAS test (with 360 ADNI AD/NC used for training).
resolution says 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch' while resolution_status is partially_resolved_candidate, and the note is a list of intermediate scores naming no separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: P-229's Table IV (MCI-to-AD, 36 months, ADNI) set against a P-178 result at a matched horizon and on a subject-level split; even then the populations (all MCI vs EMCI only) and predictor sets would differ.
